story: İğde is a WhatsApp business assistant I designed and built for my family's agriculture business. Approval requests, everyday questions, and follow-ups arrive as chat messages. İğde answers what she can on the spot and relays the rest to a human with a short note. The whole point was that the people using it never had to learn a new app.

She is fronted by İğde, an original animated character named after the oleaster fruit. Her design runs on a strict spec: only her tapered tip and gear base rotate, slowly, in one direction. Her face never turns and her mouth never moves. She communicates purely through expression, a smile and a blink. She never pretends to talk; her replies arrive as plain chat bubbles.

Her brain is relay-first by design. Short greetings and thanks get instant prepared answers in plain Turkish, a few keywords route to feasibility replies, and everything else gets a short handoff note and goes straight to a human. No live language model, nothing published without approval. Deliberately boring infrastructure around a character with real personality.
tagline: A WhatsApp business assistant with an animated avatar front.
title: İğde
